best_for: Teams already working in Slack who want the desktop app for notifications and huddles, and who know whether 90 days of history is enough before paying.

points.title: Free keeps 90 days
points.text: The free plan shows only the last 90 days of messages, allows up to 10 app integrations, limits huddles to two people, and deletes data after one year. Paid plans keep full history.

points.title: What paying costs
points.text: Pro is USD 7.25 per user per month billed yearly, or USD 8.75 billed monthly. Business+ is USD 15 per user per month billed yearly, or USD 18 monthly. Enterprise+ is quoted at USD 45 and sold through sales. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: AI is mostly a paid extra
points.text: Free and Pro get only a limited Slackbot trial. Business+ includes 15 Slackbot messages per user each week, with more bought as credits; Enterprise+ lifts the weekly cap.

points.title: New systems only
points.text: Slack lists Windows 11 23H2 or later, macOS 14 or later, and on Linux Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or later and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 or later. Older systems may still run it, but outside what Slack supports.

points.title: Windows: per-user or MSIX
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 123 versions: a per-user x64 installer that needs no admin rights, plus MSIX packages for x64 and Arm64. macOS ships separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is community-made
points.text: The Flathub package is x64 only, marked unverified, and states it is not supported by Slack. Slack itself still calls Linux a beta. macOS and Linux list only the current release here, so downgrades there need another source.
